context:
Build the explorer as a standalone subsite under the BenchBox public domain.
Prefer static or precomputed routes for canonical result pages, then add
richer browser-side interactivity on top of the derived read model.
description:
BenchBox needs a public-facing results explorer that feels like a product, not
a directory listing of JSON files. The explorer should live at
`benchbox.dev/results/`, integrate with the existing public site, and provide
stable result pages, browse flows, and compare surfaces over derived
public read models.

**Phase assignment:** This is the Phase 1 core deliverable. It does NOT depend
on the hosted governance model or full ingest architecture - Phase 1 uses a
static build pipeline (canonical bundles → JSON manifests + DuckDB snapshot)
deployed to GitHub Pages. The governance and ingest TODOs were removed as
blockers because Phase 1 is entirely maintainer-curated with no hosted services.

This TODO is a **tracking umbrella** for the Phase 1 implementation. It does
not contain implementation work itself - it mirrors the milestone state of the
results-explorer cluster. Mark each work unit done when the corresponding
cluster item(s) are completed. Mark this item Completed when w3 is done.

Note: resolve-results-explorer-brand-ownership must be resolved before launch
but does not block implementation. BenchBox placement is the working default.

anti_patterns.dont: hide the canonical raw bundle behind a UI-only representation
anti_patterns.instead: make the underlying bundle downloadable from result pages

anti_patterns.dont: use hash-only routing for canonical public result URLs
anti_patterns.instead: use real result paths or pre-rendered files
anti_patterns.why: stable shareable pages matter for a benchmark site

preserves.behavior: Explorer result pages link back to the canonical raw bundle and do not invent a second source of truth
Landing page, docs, and blog remain deployable under the existing GitHub Pages workflow until the new explorer is proven

verifications.command: test -d results-explorer/dist/ && test -f results-explorer/dist/index.html && echo PRESENT
verifications.description: Explorer Vite build output exists with an index

verifications.command: cd landing && npm run build 2>&1 | grep -c '[Ee]rror' || echo 0
verifications.description: Existing docs and landing pages build cleanly after explorer is integrated
